data.title: Pilot a code migration on one representative slice
data.summary: Establish a small before/after baseline before applying a mechanical change across a codebase.

facts.text: Claude Code documents small refactoring increments with behavior-preservation checks. Large migrations still need their own scope, orchestration and review controls.

prerequisites: Access to Claude Code; check account, client and workspace availability.
Target API/pattern, compatibility requirements and files in scope.
steps: Search for an existing migration script or partial rollout before designing another.
Choose one representative slice and capture the old behavior.
Apply the smallest transformation and inspect each changed call site.
Run compatibility and edge-case checks; record exceptions instead of forcing the transformation.
Use the pilot receipt to decide whether a broader rollout is justified. Keep production release under existing project controls.
data.output: a reviewed pilot diff, compatibility results and exception inventory
validation: Stop the rollout and revise the migration contract.
Reuse its implementation after checking current callers and tests.
limitations: Sintra-authored procedure based on provider documentation or demonstrations; no execution in the named app was performed.
Availability and results depend on your inputs, enabled tools and permissions; a suggested practice result is not a measured outcome.
data.prompt: For [migration contract], locate an existing script or partial rollout before creating another. Choose one representative slice with a difficult caller and record its current behavior. Propose a small compatible transformation, apply it in the authorized review copy and run the agreed normal/edge/error checks. Return the diff, compatibility results, exception list and recommendation on expanding the rollout. Do not perform a bulk migration or release from the pilot alone.
tips: Choose the awkward caller for the pilot, not only the easy one.
Record which changes are mechanical and which require a design decision.
